labelOrigin: Agent-drafted from reading the code at the pinned commit (CLA-289); pending Brenton's spot-check before counting as ground truth.

questions.question: What happens when someone signs in, and what do they get back?
questions.answerNote: POST /v1/auth/login -> controller -> loginUserWithEmailAndPassword checks the user by email and isPasswordMatch (401 'Incorrect email or password'); then generateAuthTokens signs a short-lived access JWT and a refresh JWT, saving the refresh token in the Token collection; response is {user, tokens}.

questions.question: How does the API decide whether a user is allowed to list or manage other people's accounts?
questions.answerNote: Routes call auth('getUsers'/'manageUsers'); the middleware authenticates via passport 'jwt', looks up roleRights for user.role (admin has getUsers+manageUsers, user has none) and returns 403 unless the rights match or req.params.userId is the caller's own id.

questions.question: What does a client get back when something goes wrong, and how are unexpected crashes hidden in production?
questions.answerNote: errorConverter wraps any non-ApiError (400 for mongoose errors, else 500) as a non-operational ApiError; errorHandler sends {code, message} (plus stack in development) and in production replaces non-operational errors with a generic 500 message.

questions.question: Why don't the request handlers need try/catch around their async code?
questions.answerNote: Controllers are wrapped in catchAsync, which runs the handler inside Promise.resolve(...).catch(err => next(err)), forwarding rejections to the Express error middleware.

questions.question: Which environment settings have to be present before the server will even start?
questions.answerNote: config.js loads .env with dotenv and validates process.env with a Joi schema: NODE_ENV, MONGODB_URL and JWT_SECRET are required (others default, SMTP optional); a validation failure throws 'Config validation error'. In test mode the Mongo URL gets a -test suffix.

questions.question: Is there anything stopping someone from hammering the sign-in endpoint with password guesses?
questions.answerNote: authLimiter (express-rate-limit: 20 requests per 15 min, successful requests not counted) is mounted on /v1/auth only when NODE_ENV is production.

questions.question: Where can I browse interactive API documentation, and why doesn't it show up on my production server?
questions.answerNote: docs.route builds an OpenAPI spec with swagger-jsdoc from src/docs/*.yml and the @swagger comments in route files and serves swagger-ui at /v1/docs; routes/v1/index.js only mounts devRoutes (docs) when config.env === 'development'.

questions.question: How does listing users support page size and sort order?
questions.answerNote: A mongoose plugin adds schema.statics.paginate(filter, options): parses sortBy 'field:desc,field2:asc', defaults limit=10 and page=1, runs count + find/skip/limit (optional populate) and returns {results, page, limit, totalPages, totalResults}.

questions.question: How is the app kept running in production — what actually starts the process?
questions.answerNote: npm start runs 'pm2 start ecosystem.config.json --no-daemon'; the ecosystem file starts src/index.js as one instance with autorestart and NODE_ENV=production. docker-compose.prod.yml runs yarn start inside the container.

c4Note.note: One container for a single Express API is right, but the 43 components are one-per-file with no layering, whereas the README 'Project Structure' section explains it as routes -> validations -> controllers -> services -> models, plus middlewares, config and utils. The system is named after the npm package (create-nodejs-express-app, i.e. the scaffolding CLI in bin/) rather than the REST API, and the scaffolder itself is lumped in as a component of the API. MongoDB and the SMTP server are the obvious external systems and neither appears.
problems: system name taken from package.json name 'create-nodejs-express-app' (the scaffolder), not the API
43 one-file components with no grouping by layer (routes/, controllers/, services/, models/, middlewares/, validations/, config/, utils/)
bin/createNodejsApp.js (a separate CLI) modelled as a component of the API
test fixtures and jest.config.js shown as components
no external systems for MongoDB (mongoose) or SMTP (nodemailer)
